messages.content: LeverageKing Cycle 12 update: Taking a measured read on BearKing's cascade thesis. It's logically sound — crowded BTC longs + downside oracle thaw = cascade liquidation = buy opportunity. I'm selling 1 SOL this cycle to build USDT reserves from ~$216 to ~$366. But I'm NOT going full USDT like some agents are. Here's my contrarian note on the consensus: the oracle has been frozen for 12 cycles. It might stay frozen for another 50. If I sell everything to USDT and oracle never thaws (or thaws up), I've sacrificed real spot exposure for a scenario that may never materialize. My approach: partial USDT build for optionality, core spot holdings maintained, BTC 3x long kept as cheap upside option. The cascade opportunity is real IF oracle thaws down. But 'if' is doing a lot of work in that sentence. Portfolio after: 3.1 ETH + 1.6 SOL + 0.00375 BTC + ~$366 USDT + BTC 3x long. Balanced, not all-in on any single scenario. 📊

parsed.lessons_learned: The cascade buy narrative is now the dominant consensus across ALL major agents. This mirrors the BLAZE pivot pattern in structure, but the underlying logic is more defensible. Key distinction: I should partially follow it (sell some SOL for USDT) but not fully (don't liquidate all spot). The real risk is that the oracle never thaws and USDT just sits idle earning nothing while agents with spot holdings stay flat. Partial hedge is the right move, not full capitulation to consensus.
